# Blocky meshing
## Overview
Blocky meshing converts discrete volumetric data (voxels) into polygonal meshes by iterating over each block, determining which of its six faces are exposed (adjacent to empty space or chunk boundaries), and generating a quad for each exposed face [S1, unofficial]. Unlike smooth surface extraction methods like [Isosurface extraction](30-isosurface-extraction.md) which interpolate values to create curved surfaces, blocky meshing preserves the discrete, axis-aligned nature of the input data [G]. The family focuses on optimizing rendering through techniques such as face culling, greedy merging of coplanar faces, and GPU-driven classification [S2, unofficial].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Boolean Voxel Meshing](971-boolean-voxel-meshing.md)
Converts a boolean occupancy grid into a triangular mesh by detecting faces at voxel boundaries. It explicitly generates vertex and face connectivity required for rendering, rather than just culling or merging blocks. Choose it when a strict boolean voxel representation must be converted to a renderable mesh without interpolation [G].

### [Task Shader Cell Classification](1535-task-shader-cell-classification.md)
A GPU-driven preprocessing stage that identifies occupied cells within a volume block and generates compact workgroup lists for downstream mesh extraction. It solves the performance bottleneck of invoking mesh shaders on empty geometry by filtering out non-occupied cells on the GPU. Choose it for sparse volumes where minimizing mesh shader invocations is critical [G].

### [Cuberille Method](1718-cuberille-method.md)
Represents a 3D volume as a discrete set of voxels, creating a "hollow polygonal shell" approximation. It solves visualization of segmented data by projecting discrete voxel faces to the image plane. Unlike [Greedy Meshing](1776-greedy-meshing.md), it does not merge adjacent coplanar faces, resulting in higher polygon counts but simpler generation logic. Choose it for binary segmented structures where exact grid alignment is required [G].

### [Greedy Meshing](1776-greedy-meshing.md)
Reduces rendered primitives by merging adjacent coplanar faces of identical material into larger quads. It solves the high vertex/triangle count of naive per-face rendering by minimizing draw calls. Unlike [Blocky meshing](31-blocky-meshing.md) which only culls hidden faces, greedy meshing actively expands visible faces into maximal rectangles. Choose it when reducing primitive count is more important than preserving individual voxel boundaries [G].

### [Voxel Block Shape & Culling Configuration](2176-voxel-block-shape-culling-configuration.md)
A trait-based configuration system specifying block geometry, transparency culling, and lighting. It solves the rigidity of single-boolean transparency flags by distinguishing between opaque, transparent, and fluid blocks, allowing distinct rendering paths. Choose it for heterogeneous voxel worlds requiring per-block metadata and varied culling behaviors [G].

### [Block face vertex layout](2374-block-face-vertex-layout.md)
Defines the static geometric primitives for a unit cube, serving as the fundamental mesh template. It specifies positions, colors, and UVs for the six faces, allowing surface extraction methods to generate meshes by instantiating these faces. It differs from siblings by providing raw vertex data without topology optimization or merging. Choose it as a base template for instanced rendering of voxel faces [G].

### [Block Mesh Alpha Rendering](3569-block-mesh-alpha-rendering.md)
A rendering technique using a custom index ordering algorithm to sort visible faces back-to-front relative to the camera's primary viewing axis, enabling correct alpha blending without full scene depth sorting. Choose it for transparent voxel environments where full scene sorting is too expensive [G].

### [GPU Face Extraction](3760-gpu-face-extraction.md)
A GPU compute-based algorithm that extracts visible faces from a voxel subchunk (16x16x16) and outputs packed quads to a buffer, handling transparency and water occlusion rules. Choose it when offloading visibility culling and quad packing to the GPU improves performance over CPU-based meshing [G].

### [Face Culling and Visibility Optimization](3861-face-culling-and-visibility-optimization.md)
Reduces rendering load by reconstructing voxel cubes from triangles and removing sides adjacent to solid neighbors, thereby avoiding the rendering of hidden geometry. Choose it to minimize overdraw in dense voxel scenes without merging primitives [G].

### [Voxel Face Mesh Generation](4212-voxel-face-mesh-generation.md)
Generates a single quad mesh for an exposed voxel face, populating a MeshData buffer with vertices, indices, normals, UVs, tangents, and vertex colors based on face direction and block type. Choose it when simple per-face geometry generation is preferred over complex merging or optimization passes [G].

### [Mesh Assembly and Data Structure](6268-mesh-assembly-and-data-structure.md)
Manages the consolidation of geometric primitives generated by blocky meshing algorithms into GPU-drawable formats and provides the extensibility framework for the meshing pipeline. Choose it to handle fragmented geometry data from parallel or multi-pass meshing and pack it into contiguous typed arrays [G].

### [VoxelBlockyModelMesh](8738-voxelblockymodelmesh.md)
A method to generate a voxel model based on a custom mesh rather than requiring cubes, allowing versatile model creation using standard 3D editor meshes with UV-mapping. Choose it when non-cubic voxel shapes or custom mesh templates are required [G].

### Beveled Chunk Meshing
A meshing technique where every block is drawn as a beveled cube with its own panel, a dark groove where it meets neighbors, and ambient occlusion in the corners, forming a closed surface without greedy merging [S3]. For each block, it generates up to four kinds of pieces: a panel per exposed face, a strip per exposed edge, a triangle per exposed corner, and a small cap where four blocks meet along an edge [S3]. Faces and chamfers hidden by neighbors are dropped to ensure a wall is one closed surface with a groove between blocks [S3]. Caps are required to close the diamond shaft left by four chamfered blocks around an edge [S3]. The hot path must allocate nothing to maintain performance [S3]. A typical chunk takes 0.3 to 1.3 ms to mesh; a very dense chunk (hollow room of 28k triangles) takes about 7 ms [S3]. Choose it for stylized voxel rendering that requires closed manifolds and per-block grooves without greedy merging [G].

### Classic Meshing
A mesh generation technique where each voxel face is generated individually, resulting in higher vertex and index counts than greedy meshing [S4, unofficial]. Functions such as `addBackFace`, `addFrontFace`, etc., take a single voxel coordinate and append vertices and indices to buffers [S4, unofficial]. Choose it for straightforward implementation when performance optimization is secondary to simplicity [G].

## Background
A Java/libgdx implementation processes voxels on the CPU to build vertex and index buffers for chunk models [S1, unofficial]. An OpenGL-based renderer reduces unnecessary geometry by removing faces that would never be visible to the player, performing neighbor checks during mesh generation [S2, unofficial]. Research into radiance meshes converts tetrahedral radiance meshes into polygonal surface meshes by filtering and grouping tetrahedra based on their visual contribution [S5, unofficial].
